asked every hospital to describe its data: Please describe your local data for the shared heart-disease prediction task (target: angiographic disease, num > 0). Focus on feature availability, missingness, value ranges/units, any broken or ambiguous values, and any site-specific quirks that could affect a shared feature contract.

This hospital contributes 181 training rows with a label-positive rate of about 46%. Data are largely clean: no columns contain physiologically impossible zero values (age, trestbps, chol, thalach all have positive minima), so no zero_means_missing rules are needed. Only 'ca' (1 missing) and 'thal' (2 missing) have any missingness, which is already represented as '?' in the export. All categorical codes (cp, restecg, slope, ca, thal) fall within their documented value sets.

Budapest has 176 training rows, 36% label-positive. Missing values are encoded as '?' already, so no zero-means-missing columns were found; all 0 values in sex/fbs/restecg/exang/oldpeak are genuine. The main site-specific quirks are heavy missingness: ca is ~99% missing (only 2 usable rows) and should be dropped, thal is ~87% missing, and slope ~63% missing; chol (~6%) and fbs (~4%) are partly missing. All continuous clinical ranges look physiologically plausible, with only a rare high cholesterol (518 mg/dl).

Zurich/Basel has only 73 training rows, and the label is heavily skewed: 94.5% of patients have angiographic heart disease, so this site contributes almost no negative examples. Serum cholesterol (chol) is entirely recorded as 0 and therefore unusable; ca (fluoroscopy vessel count) is 96% missing and fbs is 60% missing. oldpeak contains negative ST-depression values that are not physiologically possible and must be treated as missing via a valid_range rule (min 0).

VA Long Beach contributes 120 training rows with a high label-positive rate (74.2% angiographic disease). The most usable features are age, sex, cp, restecg, and fbs (complete); trestbps, thalach, exang, and oldpeak have ~26-28% missingness but remain usable; chol needs zero-to-missing correction (28 zero-coded values). ca (99.2% missing), thal (83.3% missing), and slope (52.5% missing) are too sparse to be useful here.

proposal 1: 9 features (age, sex, cp, trestbps, fbs, restecg, thalach, exang, oldpeak); 4 quality rules — Use features that are reasonably available and clinically meaningful at all four sites. Drop ca (96-99% missing at three sites), thal (41-87% missing at three sites), slope (52-63% missing at two sites) and chol (all zero/missing at Zurich-Basel and heavily zero-coded at VA) so no missingness indicator becomes a constant site proxy. Keep numeric/binary/categorical features with mean imputation only, plus physiological range rules for age, trestbps, thalach and oldpeak (negative oldpeak treated as missing).

accepted the contract — All nine contracted features are fully available at this hospital with zero missing after the physiological range rules, and the categorical codes for cp/restecg fall within documented value sets. We note that ca, thal, slope, and chol are well-populated here (chol range 126-417, ca/thal only ~0.6-1% missing), so dropping them costs local predictive signal, but the coordinator's cross-site rationale (those columns are largely missing or zero-coded at other sites and would act as constant site proxies) is sound, so we accept.

accepted the contract — All nine retained features are available and meaningful at Budapest (only fbs has ~4% missing, imputed by mean). Dropping ca (99% missing locally), thal (~87%) and slope (~63%) matches our data; dropping chol is acceptable since other sites cannot provide it meaningfully. The range rules are consistent with our reported values.

accepted the contract — The contract drops the columns my site cannot provide (chol fully zero, ca 96% missing) and applies the correct oldpeak valid_range rule (negative values now treated as missing, 16% of my rows). One caveat rather than a blocker: fbs is 60% missing at my site and mean-imputation will fill most of it with a constant, so it contributes little local signal here, but the feature still has both 0 and 1 values present and is usable elsewhere. Accepting.
